title: Add types to totalPrice
quote: Turning on the noImplicitAny flag will issue an error on any variables whose type is implicitly inferred as any.

back:
No. `count = "five"` fails: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'. The label lines compile.

Why: count was inferred as number from its initial value, and that type sticks. label had no initial value, so its type follows each assignment.

Docs: TypeScript Handbook — The Basics — https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/basic-types.html
quote: In many cases, TypeScript can even just infer (or "figure out") the types for us even if we omit them.
